Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us Considered an "Enemy Race" in Their Own Country This is how Western Defense Commander John L. DeWitt characterized people of Japanese ancestry during World War II. He insisted that even those who had been born and raised as U.S. citizens nevertheless posed a threat because their Japanese “racial strains” were “undiluted.” Under the authority of President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Executive Order 9066, DeWitt ordered the removal of all Japanese Americans from the West Coast in 1942. Allowed to take only what they could carry, they were imprisoned, without trial, in some of the most desolate places in the country. Today, the National Park Service preserves those sites so that visitors may learn their story. Jeffrey Novak Principal Deputy General Counsel Novak was appointed Principal Deputy General Counsel in May 2025 and served as Acting General Counsel until October 2025. He is an Honors College graduate of Ball State University and a graduate of the Indiana University School of Law. During law school, Novak worked as a law clerk for Bill Cummings, formerly the United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia. After graduating law school, he served a two-year clerkship with the late Charles R. Richey, United States District Judge for the District of Columbia, before joining McGuire Woods, where he was elected to partnership. Before joining the Department, he worked in a variety of roles at technology companies over the course of more than 20 years, including managing litigation, compliance, patent, and public policy functions, while also serving on the boards of the Northern Virginia Technology Council, the Internet Association, and the Virginia Early Childhood Foundation.

In this position, he is responsible for the full range of human capital services covering DOE's workforce of 13,000 Federal employees. Working with the Chief Human Capital Officer, he sets strategic direction and programmatic priorities for the human capital organization and provides leadership across a myriad of teams responsible for DOE workforce planning, advisory services, hiring, benefits, policy, employee and labor relations, executive resources management, talent management, engagement, human resources information technology, and accountability. He provides oversight to shared service centers supporting DOE Headquarters, national program offices, and power administrations. Jeff has over 30 years of Federal service and has been with the Department of Energy since 2009. Jeff has served in various senior leadership positions within Human Capital to include four Shared Service Centers (SSCs) and the Office of Business Operations. The company said its mains gas, mini bulk tank and cylinder tariffs would increase by 1p per kilowatt hour (kWh) for all domestic and commercial customers from 1 December 2026. It said the increase reflected higher wholesale gas and liquefied petroleum gas costs amid disruption to exports and shipping routes in the Middle East after the conflict with Iran. Chief executive Graeme Millar said: "We recognise that any price increase is unwelcome, particularly during winter." Close jfd553's Diary Mapping Icefields Parkway, Part 1: A two-year mapping journey Posted by jfd553 on 4 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 6 November 2026. I spent two years mapping the areas surrounding one of the most beautiful drives in the world. Each morning, I looked forward to discovering and mapping an area adjacent to a one I did the day before. This diary entry serves as an introduction to a series of texts covering the challenges I encountered and how I overcame them. Included below are a few snapshots taken in the field, which capture the majestic landscapes along the Icefields Parkway. I have also added a “before and after” map excerpt, as well as a short video, to illustrate how my work gradually took shape over time. The Place The Icefields Parkway (Highway 93N), in Alberta, owes its name to the spectacular icefields and glaciers that line the road. The parkway, which is a 232 km stretch of highway cutting through Banff and Jasper National Parks, attracts between 1.2 million and 2 million visitors per year. The parkway offers exceptional alpine landscape, with glaciers, rivers, turquoise lakes, and breathtaking mountain views directly from the roadside (Figure 1). Best of all, many of these landmarks can be reached in a single day’s hike (Figure 2). Figure 1: North Saskatchewan River alongside the parkway. Jungle: Tiny Desk Concert November 2, 2026 5:00 AM ET Robin Hilton Credit: Photo: Lexy Beale/NPR It's hard for any band to make the old sound completely new, but Jungle has spent much of the past decade transforming vintage soul and R&B into something almost alien. The grooves are deep and warmly familiar, with wistful reflections on love and longing. But even in the brightest moments, there's often a thread of mystery and melancholy that leaves you questioning whether everything is as it seems. Fronted by the trio of Tom McFarland, Josh Lloyd-Watson and Lydia Kitto, Jungle is known for fluid live sets, with songs that spill into each other. True to form, at the Tiny Desk, they perform more than a half-dozen tracks that run together in a single, continuous groove. "We're gonna keep the music rolling," Lloyd-Watson tells the NPR crowd as the band melts seamlessly from 2018's "Beat 54 (All Good Now)" into "Dominoes" from the 2023 album Volcano. pages.text: Jurassic period information and facts | National Geographic SCIENCE What is the Jurassic period and why did it end? The heyday of dinosaurs, the Jurassic era saw Earth’s climate change from hot and dry to humid and subtropical. The Jurassic period was characterized by a warm, wet climate that gave rise to lush vegetation and abundant life. Many new dinosaurs emerged—in great numbers. Above, Dimorphodon reptiles fly over a herd of Mamenchisaurus dinosaurs coming down to a river for a drink. Illustration by CoreyFord, Getty Images By National Geographic Staff Last updated August 18, 2025 The Jurassic is a geologic period that took place about 201.3 million years to 145 million years ago and constitutes the middle part of the Mesozoic era . The Jurassic period was named after the Jura limestone deposits in the Jura Mountains, discovered by German geologist Alexander von Humboldt . Building on this find, French scientist Alexandre Brongniart later coined the Jurassic period. There are three Jurassic time periods: early, middle, and late. Overall, the Jurassic gives us a particularly well-preserved fossil record of prehistoric life, which included theropod dinosaurs that scientists believe evolved to become birds . Thanks to this rich record, we know that the Jurassic was the age of dinosaurs roaming a tropical Earth filled with ferns, flowering plants, and conifers. It was also a time when sea monsters, sharks, and blood-red plankton filled inland seas borne of crumbling landmasses. Here’s what the Jurassic period was really like. Justin Bis Justin Bis is the Chief of Staff for the Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC) at the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). In this role, he works alongside OTC leadership to maximize the impact of DOE’s investments in technology commercialization, strengthen coordination across the agency, and ensure long-term success. He previously served at the White House as Special Assistant to President Trump and Deputy Director of the Presidential Personnel Office, where he managed the appointment of senior government officials responsible for regulating the U.S. financial and energy markets. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn K2-Play Completes Final Phase of North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan Oct 15, 2026 FRUITA, Colo. – Over the past eight years, the North Fruita Desert has changed in ways riders can see as soon as they arrive. There are more miles of singletrack, more places to camp and dedicated space for races and other large events, all part of a broader effort by the Bureau of Land Management and community partners to keep pace with one of western Colorado’s busiest recreation areas. This fall, the final trail in the North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan is complete. K2-Play winds for about three miles along the base of the Book Cliffs and completes the final phase of a roughly 30-mile expansion of the 18 Road trail system. Its completion caps years of planning and construction involving the BLM Grand Junction Field Office, Colorado Plateau Mountain Bike Trail Association, Mesa County, City of Fruita, local businesses, professional trail builders and volunteers. Before coming to DOE, Katie served for 12 years at the Department of Health and Human Services where she focused on policy and budget development at the international, intergovernmental, interagency and congressional levels. He works with America’s allies and partners to expand markets for American energy and technology, strengthen energy security, counter malign foreign influence, and promote access to affordable, reliable, and secure energy around the world. pages.text: Khawaja book: Sandpapergate a stench Cricket Australia cannot shake - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Pat Cummins has led Australia in 43 Tests since 2021 By Stephan Shemilt Cricket Correspondent Published 10 November 2026 There are stories that can damage reputations, tarnish legacies and put asterisks next to achievements. Never-ending sagas, claim and counterclaim, one word against another. Are Pep Guardiola's trophies at Manchester City rendered worthless by financial rule breaches? Phil Westcott From Juneau, to Anchorage, to Nome, and beyond, people in Alaska are often spotted wearing a colorful or patterned hooded garment with a big front pocket. This classic Alaska attire is known as a kuspuk. Kuspuk is an English word based on the Indigenous Yup’ik word “qaspeq” which translates to “cloth over parka.” The original qaspeq was made from gut skin, animal hide, or feathered bird skin to keep the wearer warm and dry—a constant struggle known all too well by those who have live, work, and travel in the arctic. In the 1800s, European whalers brought goods to trade, which included cloth bags filled with flour or sugar. Indigenous (Inupiaq/Yup’ik) women repurposed the cotton flour sacks and sewed a lightweight summer garment that resembled the “over parkas” worn in the winter.Today, kuspuks are often made of colorful or patterned cotton material and are locally hand-made. La influenza y el embarazo 17 de sep. del 2024 English (US) Lo que debe saber La influenza (gripe) durante el embarazo tiene más probabilidades de causar una enfermedad que requiera hospitalización. Si está embarazada y tiene síntomas de influenza, llame a su proveedor de atención médica inmediatamente. Los CDC recomiendan un pronto tratamiento antiviral contra la influenza durante el embarazo para las personas con influenza confirmada o presunta. La influenza y el embarazo La influenza también podría ser dañina para el bebé en gestación durante el embarazo. This fellowship provides innovators who have early-stage energy startups and/or emerging technologies with the support needed to develop and transition their ideas into the market. These entrepreneurs are embedded for a period of two years at one of four national labs where they are mentored by a lab scientist. pages.text: Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum | National Geographic 1:00 Artist's impression of the Ichthyosaurus ILLUSTRATION BY JOSCHUA KNÜPPE Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum The paleontologist who made the discovery was originally at the museum to study a fossil that resembles the Loch Ness monster. By Sarah Gibbens Published August 28, 2017 • 4 min read Sven Sachs, a paleontologist from the Bielefeld Natural History Museum in Germany, was at the Lower Saxony State Museum in Hannover to study an ancient sea reptile when one of the museum's display fossils caught his eye. The specimen had originally been unearthed in the mid-1990s in Somerset, England, but it had remained largely unstudied since. Sachs suspected it was an Ichthyosaurus. Commonly mistaken for a dinosaur, the species was more like a "sea dragon" marine reptile that had a long, flexible body and may have swum like eels. "I found it very extraordinary," said Sachs. "[It was] way bigger than any specimen I had examined." He explained the specimen had previously been labeled as a smaller species within the Ichthyosaurus group. Sachs reached out to Ichthyosaurus expert Dean Lomax from the University of Manchester, and in early 2017 they examined the specimen together, finding it to be a specimen of the species Ichthyosaurus somersetensis . Skeleton of Ichthyosaurus . Photograph by Dean Lomax Their findings, published in the journal Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , describe the largest known specimen of its kind. pages.text: Laws | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Laws Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959, as amended (LMRDA) Law ( PDF ) Regulations OLMS Interpretative Manual Synopsis of Law The Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959, as amended (LMRDA), grants certain rights to union members and protects their interests by promoting democratic procedures within labor organizations. The LMRDA establishes: A Bill of Rights for union members; Reporting requirements for labor organizations, union officers and employees, employers, labor-relations consultants, and surety companies; Standards for the regular election of union officers; and Safeguards for protecting labor organization funds and assets. The Secretary of Labor enforces certain provisions of the LMRDA and has delegated that authority to the Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) of the Department of Labor. Other provisions may only be enforced by union members through a private suit in a Federal district court. The Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 (CSRA) Standards of Conduct Law Regulations Synopsis of Law The Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 (CSRA) applies to labor organizations which represents employees in most agencies of the executive branch of the Federal Government. The regulations implementing the standards of conduct provisions of the CSRA incorporate many LMRDA provisions, including those related to labor organization reporting requirements.
